vieille: The old town on the hill of the left bank: the Bourg-de-Four square with its fountain, the Grand-Rue where Jean-Jacques Rousseau was born, the Hôtel de Ville with the Arsenal and its cannons, and the Promenade de la Treille with its very long bench under the trees. Wander slowly among lanes and little squares.
cattedrale: St Pierre Cathedral and its towers

The great cathedral where Calvin preached, a short walk from the Bourg-de-Four: inside are the Gothic nave and "Calvin's chair". You can climb the north tower (157 steps) for a 360-degree view over the city, the lake and, in good weather, Mont Blanc. Beneath the church is an important archaeological site.
bastions: Parc des Bastions and the Reformation Wall

The park below the old town walls, with giant outdoor chess and the Reformation Wall, a hundred-metre frieze with statues of Farel, Calvin, Beza and Knox, the leading figures of the Protestant Reformation. Opposite is the University's historic building.
rade: Geneva's symbol: a 140-metre jet of water rising from the lake. Walk there along the lakefront, past the Pont du Mont-Blanc and the Jardin Anglais with its famous flower clock. The little boats (Mouettes genevoises) that cross the harbour also leave from here, included in the public transport ticket.
paquis: Bains des Pâquis and the jetty

The public baths on the lake, loved by Genevans: a jetty reaching into the water with a lighthouse, a view of the Jet d'Eau and Mont Blanc, the buvette and, in winter, a sauna and hammam. In summer people dive off the jetty; in autumn and winter they come for fondue and the walk.
mah: The city's largest museum, with art, archaeology and applied arts: paintings by Hodler and other Swiss and European artists, armour, Konrad Witz's famous altarpiece and collections from Egypt to modern Switzerland.
patek: The Patek Philippe watchmaking museum: five centuries of pocket watches and wristwatches, automata, enamels and unique pieces, in a building in Plainpalais. The place to understand why Geneva is the watch capital.
croce: The museum devoted to the history of the Red Cross and Red Crescent, founded in Geneva by Henry Dunant: with photos, objects and stories of wars and rescues, a moving and easy-to-follow visit. It's opposite the Palace of Nations.
onu: Palais des Nations and the Broken Chair

The European headquarters of the United Nations, in a large park: the guided tour of about an hour takes you into the assembly and council halls. In front, on Place des Nations, is the Broken Chair, the giant chair with a broken leg, a symbol against landmines, which you can photograph for free at any time.
cern: The visitor centre of CERN, the European particle physics laboratory: interactive exhibitions on accelerators, particles and the universe, scientific installations and a café. Entry is free. From Geneva, take tram 18 to the CERN terminus.
carouge: A town founded by the King of Sardinia in the 18th century, now part of Geneva: straight streets, low houses in warm colours, tree-lined squares, craft workshops and cafés. It has a Savoyard, slightly Italian feel, very different from the centre.
